chapter: Ch 7: Accounting Standards Based on Items Impacting Financial Statements
unit: Unit 3: AS 11 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Scope and Applicability of AS 11
explain: AS 11 applies to accounting for transactions denominated in foreign currencies.
It governs the translation of financial statements of foreign operations like branches or subsidiaries.
It includes accounting for forward exchange contracts.
It does not specify the presentation currency, but Indian companies normally present financial statements in INR.
It excludes cash flow statement presentation of foreign currency cash flows, which is covered under AS 3.
It excludes exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings to the extent they are treated as interest adjustments under AS 16.

flow.title: Checking Scope of AS 11
steps: Identify foreign currency transactions or operations
Check if covered by AS 11 scope
Apply AS 11 translation rules
Exclude AS 3 cash flows and AS 16 borrowing costs

topics.example: An Indian company exporting software to the US and billing in USD must apply AS 11 to record sales and receivables in INR.
remember: AS 11 does not prescribe presentation currency, but statutory requirements in India mandate INR.
mistakes: Including cash flow translation under AS 11 instead of AS 3.

quiz.q: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of AS 11?
o: Presentation of foreign currency cash flows in Cash Flow Statement
quiz.why: Presentation of foreign currency cash flows in the cash flow statement is governed by AS 3, not AS 11.

quiz.q: Does AS 11 mandate a specific presentation currency for financial statements?
o: No, it does not specify presentation currency
quiz.why: AS 11 does not specify the currency in which an enterprise presents its financial statements, though Indian entities normally use INR.

topics.title: Key Definitions in AS 11
explain: Foreign Currency Transaction: A transaction denominated in or requiring settlement in a foreign currency.
Monetary Items: Money held and assets or liabilities to be received or paid in fixed or determinable amounts of money.
Non-Monetary Items: Assets and liabilities other than monetary items, such as fixed assets or inventory.
Foreign Operation: A subsidiary, associate, joint venture, or branch whose activities are conducted in another country.
Net Investment in Foreign Operation: The reporting enterprise's share in the net assets of a non-integral foreign operation.

flow.title: Classifying an Item as Monetary or Non-Monetary
steps: Check item in financial statements
Is amount fixed or determinable in money?
If Yes, classify as Monetary Item
If No, classify as Non-Monetary Item

topics.example: Cash, trade receivables, and trade payables are monetary items. Fixed assets, inventory, and equity investments are non-monetary items.
remember: Advances paid for purchase of fixed assets/goods are non-monetary because they result in receipt of assets/goods, not fixed cash.
mistakes: Treating trade receivables or creditors as non-monetary items.

quiz.q: Which of the following is classified as a monetary item under AS 11?
quiz.why: Trade receivables represent a right to receive a fixed amount of money, making them a monetary item.

quiz.q: What defines a non-monetary item under AS 11?
o: Assets to be received in fixed amounts of cash
Assets and liabilities other than monetary items
Liabilities to be paid in fixed cash amounts
quiz.why: Non-monetary items are defined by AS 11 as assets and liabilities other than monetary items.

topics.title: Initial Recognition of Foreign Currency Transactions
explain: A foreign currency transaction is initially recorded in the reporting currency (INR).
The exchange rate applied is the spot rate between reporting currency and foreign currency at the date of transaction.
An average rate for a week or month may be used if it approximates actual rates.
If exchange rates fluctuate significantly, using an average rate is unreliable and prohibited.

flow.title: Initial Recognition Process
steps: Identify transaction in foreign currency
Obtain spot exchange rate on transaction date
Multiply foreign amount by transaction rate
Record transaction in INR in accounting books

topics.example: If a company buys goods for US$ 15,000 on 1st Jan when exchange rate is ₹75/$, purchases are recorded at ₹11,25,000.
remember: Initial recognition always uses the spot exchange rate (or reliable average rate) on the transaction date.
mistakes: Recording initial purchases using year-end closing rates instead of the transaction date rate.

quiz.q: At what exchange rate is a foreign currency transaction initially recorded?
o: Rate on the date of transaction
Average rate of the year always
quiz.why: AS 11 requires foreign currency transactions to be recorded initially using the exchange rate at the date of the transaction.

quiz.q: When is the use of an average exchange rate for initial recognition unreliable?
o: When the transaction value is small
quiz.why: Significant fluctuations in exchange rates make weekly or monthly average rates unreliable.

topics.title: Reporting at Subsequent Balance Sheet Dates
explain: Foreign currency monetary items must be reported using the closing rate at the balance sheet date.
If closing rate is unrealistic or uncollectible, report monetary items at the net realizable/payable amount.
Non-monetary items carried at historical cost are reported using the exchange rate at the date of transaction.
Non-monetary items carried at fair value are reported using exchange rates existing when fair values were determined.
Contingent liabilities denominated in foreign currency are disclosed using the closing rate.

flow.title: Subsequent Reporting Valuation
steps: Identify balance sheet item type
For monetary items, apply closing rate
For historical non-monetary items, keep transaction rate
For fair value non-monetary items, apply valuation rate

topics.example: Trade receivables of $15,000 recorded initially at ₹75/$ are restated at year-end closing rate of ₹74/$, reporting ₹11,10,000.
remember: Monetary items = closing rate. Historical cost non-monetary items = transaction date rate.
mistakes: Restating fixed assets carried at historical cost using year-end closing exchange rates.

quiz.q: How are non-monetary items carried at historical cost reported at the balance sheet date?
o: At rate on date of transaction
At average rate for the period
quiz.why: Historical cost non-monetary items are reported using the exchange rate on the date of transaction.

quiz.q: At what exchange rate are foreign currency contingent liabilities disclosed?
quiz.why: Contingent liabilities denominated in foreign currency at balance sheet date are disclosed using the closing rate.

topics.title: Recognition of Exchange Differences and Para 46A Option
explain: General Rule: Exchange differences arising on settlement or reporting of monetary items are recognized as income or expense in P&L for the period.
Para 46A Option: Enterprise can choose an alternative treatment for long-term foreign currency monetary items (term of 12+ months at origination).
Depreciable Capital Assets: If long-term borrowing relates to acquiring a depreciable capital asset, exchange differences are added to or deducted from asset cost.
Other Long-Term Items: If borrowing is not for depreciable assets, differences are accumulated in Foreign Currency Monetary Item Translation Difference Account (FCMITDA).
FCMITDA balance is amortized over the balance tenure of the item and shown under 'Reserves and Surplus' on the Equity and Liabilities side.
Once exercised, the option under Para 46A is irrevocable for all long-term foreign currency monetary items.

flow.title: Accounting for Exchange Differences
steps: Calculate exchange difference on monetary item
Is Para 46A option exercised for long-term item?
If No, charge entire difference to P&L
If Yes and for depreciable asset, adjust cost
If Yes and not for asset, transfer to FCMITDA

topics.example: A long-term loan of USD 10,000 taken for purchasing machinery suffers ₹30,000 exchange loss. Under Para 46A, ₹30,000 is added to Property, Plant and Equipment cost.
remember: Long-term foreign currency monetary items must have an original term of 12 months or more. FCMITDA appears under Reserves & Surplus.
mistakes: Presenting a debit balance in FCMITDA on the asset side as an asset; Schedule III requires showing it under Reserves and Surplus.

quiz.q: Under Para 46A of AS 11, exchange differences on long-term foreign currency loans taken for acquiring depreciable assets are:
o: Added to or deducted from the cost of asset
quiz.why: Para 46A permits adjusting exchange differences arising on long-term monetary items for acquiring depreciable capital assets to the asset cost.

quiz.q: Where is the debit balance of FCMITDA presented in the Balance Sheet?
quiz.why: FCMITDA balance represents loss but is presented under 'Reserves and Surplus' on the Equity and Liabilities side per Schedule III.

topics.title: Classification and Translation of Foreign Operations
explain: Foreign Operations are classified as Integral Foreign Operations (IFO) or Non-Integral Foreign Operations (NFO).
Integral Foreign Operation (IFO): Carries business as an extension of reporting entity (e.g., branch selling goods received from HO).

IFO Translation: Individual items translated as if entered into by HO itself (monetary at closing rate, historical fixed assets at purchase rate, income/expenses at transaction/average rate). Differences go to P&L.
Non-Integral Foreign Operation (NFO): Operates autonomously, accumulates cash, incurs expenses, and generates sales in local currency.
NFO Translation: ALL assets and liabilities (monetary and non-monetary) translated at closing rate; income and expenses translated at transaction/average rate.
NFO Exchange Differences: Accumulated in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) under Shareholders' Funds until disposal of net investment.

flow.title: Translating Foreign Operations
steps: Classify operation as IFO or NFO
For IFO: Translate items individually, gain/loss to P&L
For NFO: Translate all assets and liabilities at closing rate
For NFO: Accumulate translation differences in FCTR

topics.example: A foreign branch selling goods sent by head office is an IFO (exchange difference to P&L). An independent foreign subsidiary operating locally is an NFO (exchange difference to FCTR).
remember: IFO translation differences go to Profit & Loss Account. NFO translation differences go to Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR).
mistakes: Translating fixed assets of a Non-Integral Foreign Operation at historical rates instead of closing rate.

quiz.q: Where are exchange differences arising on translation of a Non-Integral Foreign Operation (NFO) accumulated?
quiz.why: Translation differences for NFO are deferred and accumulated in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) until disposal.

quiz.q: For an Integral Foreign Operation, at what rate are fixed assets carried at historical cost translated?
o: Average exchange rate for the year
Exchange rate at the date of purchase of asset
quiz.why: For IFO, historical cost fixed assets are translated using the exchange rate at the date of acquisition.

topics.title: Accounting for Forward Exchange Contracts
explain: Forward Exchange Contract: An agreement to exchange currencies at a specified forward rate at a future date.
Hedging Contracts (Not for trading/speculation):
Premium or Discount = Difference between spot rate and forward rate at contract inception.
Premium or discount is amortized as expense or income over the life of the contract.
Exchange differences arising from rate changes during the period are recognized in Profit and Loss.
Trading / Speculation Contracts: Premium or discount is ignored. Contract is marked to market at each balance sheet date, with gains/losses recognized in P&L.

flow.title: Forward Contract Accounting Process
steps: Identify contract purpose: hedging or speculation
If Hedging: Calculate premium or discount at inception
Amortize premium or discount over contract life
Recognize exchange rate change gains/losses in P&L
If Speculation: Mark to market, net gain to P&L

topics.example: Buying a 3-month forward contract for $1,00,000 at ₹49.15 when spot rate is ₹48.85 creates a premium of ₹0.30/$, totaling ₹30,000 loss to be amortized over 3 months.
remember: Hedging contract premium/discount is amortized over contract tenure; speculation contract premium is ignored and marked to market.
mistakes: Amortizing premium or discount on forward contracts entered into for trading or speculation purposes.

quiz.q: How is premium or discount on a hedging forward exchange contract treated under AS 11?
o: Charged fully to P&L at inception
Amortized over the life of the contract
Capitalized to cost of underlying asset
quiz.why: The premium or discount arising at inception of a hedging forward contract should be amortized as expense or income over the contract life.

quiz.q: For speculative forward exchange contracts, how is gain or loss recognized at balance sheet date?
o: Premium is amortized over contract life
Contract is marked to market with gain/loss to P&L
No entry is made until final settlement
quiz.why: Speculative forward contracts ignore initial premium/discount and are marked to market at each balance sheet date with gain/loss in P&L.

topics.title: Disclosure Requirements under AS 11
explain: Enterprise must disclose the amount of exchange differences included in net profit or loss for the period.
Disclose net exchange differences accumulated in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR) and a reconciliation of FCTR from beginning to end of period.
If reporting currency differs from the currency of the country of domicile, disclose the reason for using a different currency and any change in reporting currency.
Disclose changes in classification of a foreign operation (nature, reason, impact on shareholders' funds, and impact on prior period profits).
If option under Para 46/46A is exercised, disclose the fact of exercise and unamortized amounts remaining.

flow.title: AS 11 Disclosure Checklist
steps: Report exchange differences in P&L
Reconcile opening and closing FCTR balance
State reasons if reporting currency differs from domicile
Disclose classification changes of foreign operations
Disclose Para 46A exercise and unamortized balance

topics.example: A company discloses ₹20,000 foreign exchange gain in its P&L notes and provides a reconciliation table for FCTR in shareholders' funds.
remember: Disclosure of Para 46A exercise and unamortized FCMITDA balance is mandatory in every period until fully amortized.
mistakes: Omitting disclosure of reasons when an Indian company presents financial statements in USD instead of INR.

quiz.q: What disclosure is required for Foreign Currency Translation Reserve (FCTR)?
o: A reconciliation of opening and closing FCTR balance
Names of all foreign bank accounts
quiz.why: AS 11 mandates disclosing accumulated FCTR as a separate component of shareholders' funds along with a reconciliation.

quiz.q: If an entity changes the classification of a foreign operation, it must disclose:
o: Only the new spot exchange rate
Nature, reason, and financial impact on funds and profit
quiz.why: AS 11 requires disclosing the nature, reason, impact on shareholders' funds, and impact on net profit/loss for prior periods presented.
